title: Lutnick Pushed to Weaken Chip Rules That Overlap with His Family Business
llm_summary: Sen. Richard Lutnick, whose family runs a semiconductor design firm, faced pressure from industry lobbyists to water down new U.S. chip‑export rules that would restrict sales of advanced chips to certain foreign customers. Critics say the changes would benefit his own business by keeping lucrative markets open, while supporters argue the tweaks are needed to protect American tech jobs and maintain supply‑chain competitiveness.
